stem: A hydraulic crane will lift a 17,500 lb load at a 55 ft radius. Chart values for the boom in use: 50 ft radius, 23,000 lb; 60 ft radius, 20,000 lb. Chart notes: for radii between listed values, use the next longer radius. Deduct the hook block (800 lb) and rigging (400 lb). Deduct 1,500 lb for a stowed jib or 3,000 lb for an erected jib. The jib is stowed. Can the lift be made?
choices: No; the net capacity is 17,300 lb
Yes; the net capacity is 18,800 lb
Yes; the net capacity is 20,300 lb
No; the net capacity is 15,800 lb
rationales: Use the 60 ft value: 20,000 lb. Subtract the stowed jib (1,500), hook block (800) and rigging (400): 20,000 − 2,700 = 17,300 lb. That is less than 17,500 lb, so the lift cannot be made.
This interpolates between radii: (23,000 + 20,000) ÷ 2 = 21,500, minus 2,700 = 18,800. The chart note says to use the next longer radius, not to interpolate.
This uses the shorter 50 ft radius: 23,000 − 2,700 = 20,300 lb. Capacity drops as radius grows, so the 60 ft value applies.
This uses the erected-jib deduction: 20,000 − 3,000 − 1,200 = 15,800 lb. The jib is stowed, so the deduction is 1,500 lb.
beyond: Chart notes are part of the manufacturer's limits. Skipping one deduction can turn a lift that does not work into one that looks fine on paper.
fact: Net capacity requires the next longer radius and every applicable deduction from the manufacturer's chart notes.
